summary.intent: Move the explanatory_insights live_injection feature from inline lifecycle logic to a standalone Claude Code hook, similar to the explanatory-output-style plugin, so the prompt is injected via additionalContext rather than printed as visible text.
summary.outcome: A separate SessionStart hook named 'explanatory-insights' is now installed in .claude/settings.json when live_injection is enabled; the lifecycle dispatcher was cleaned of explanatory insights logic and a new HookContextWriter implementation was added to ClaudeCodeAgent.

repo: Claude Code agents can implement HookContextWriter (WriteHookResponseWithContext) to inject additionalContext into the model's context window, vs HookResponseWriter which outputs visible systemMessage text
Built-in agents (ClaudeCode, Codex, Gemini CLI) don't use DeclaredCapabilities; As* helpers fall through to direct type assertions
Hook execution dispatched via hook_registry.go executeAgentHook; hook names registered in HookNames() on the agent
Codex and Gemini CLI already implemented HookContextWriter before this change; Claude Code was the missing implementor
InstallHooks/UninstallHooks in claudecode/hooks.go manage .claude/settings.json hook entries; a removeSpecificHookCommand helper was added to support conditional removal

code.finding: Added WriteHookResponseWithContext method and compile-time interface assertion for HookContextWriter; refactored WriteHookResponse to share a common writeHookResponse helper
InstallHooks now conditionally installs 'explanatory-insights' SessionStart hook based on live_injection setting; added removeSpecificHookCommand helper for cleanup
Added 'explanatory-insights' case to executeAgentHook dispatch and getHookType classification
New file: standalone handler handleExplanatoryInsightsHook that outputs the prompt as additionalContext JSON
Removed explanatory insights branching, prompt constant, and buildExplanatoryInsightsPrompt from writeSessionStartHookResponse; function no longer needs ctx param

workflow: Initial approach (inline lifecycle injection) was immediately revised when the user preferred a separate hook file — understanding user preference before implementation would have saved one iteration
Pre-existing lint errors in unrelated files can obscure whether new changes introduced issues; checking git diff output is the right way to confirm change scope

friction: Pre-existing lint errors in the repo made it hard to confirm at a glance whether the new changes were clean
First implementation was done inline in lifecycle.go before user clarified they wanted a separate hook file — required a full redesign pass
open_items: The HookContextWriter implementation added to ClaudeCodeAgent in lifecycle.go may now be partially redundant if all context injection goes through the standalone hook — worth reviewing whether WriteHookResponseWithContext is still needed on the agent directly
